transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi. Honestly, what made me finally make an appointment is that I just keep getting up during these really long sales strategy meetings at work. I know I’m supposed to stay seated, but... well, like last Tuesday, my manager Dave was presenting. Dave always wears these incredibly loud ties—I mean, who wears a bright yellow tie with tiny pineapples on it to a corporate meeting? It's so weird. Anyway, he was going on and on about our Q3 ad buy projections, and I just couldn't sit there anymore. 

I keep finding excuses to get up, even if it’s just to refill my water or pace by the printer. Actually, the printer jammed while I was standing next to it the other day, and I spent like twenty minutes trying to pull the paper out. It was that thick glossy brochure stock we use for the new client campaigns, which is super expensive, so I was trying really hard not to rip it, you know? The toner gets everywhere if you aren't careful. But yeah... I just can't seem to stay in my chair during those meetings when I know I'm supposed to.
When you’re in a meeting, do you usually feel restless or physically driven to get up and move around?

I'm not really sure if I'd say I feel physically driven, or... I don't know if I've ever really noticed feeling restless exactly. Maybe it's partly because the chairs in Conference Room B are just incredibly uncomfortable? They have these weird mesh backs that are supposed to be ergonomic, but they just catch on everything. 

I actually ruined a really nice cashmere cardigan on one of those chairs last winter. It was my favorite one, too—this deep plum color I got at the Nordstrom half-yearly sale. I always try to make it to that sale because you can find amazing deals on professional clothes, and in ad sales, you really have to look put together for the clients, you know? First impressions are everything. But anyway, yeah, I'm not sure about feeling a physical drive to move, I just know I end up standing up a lot.
Before age 15, did you often do things like lie, steal, break rules, or get into fights on purpose?

No, I don't think so. I was actually a pretty good kid. I mean, I definitely talked too much in class—my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, used to move my desk right next to hers because I wouldn't stop chatting with my best friend Sarah. Sarah and I are actually still friends, believe it or not. She just had her second baby, a little boy, and I went to her baby shower last weekend. It was one of those brunch things with a waffle bar, which was amazing, but they played all these weird baby shower games that I am just terrible at. Like the one where you have to guess what kind of chocolate bar is melted in the diaper? Honestly, it's a little gross if you think about it too much. But anyway, no, I didn't steal or get into fights or anything like that. I just talked a lot.
Do you often have trouble paying close attention to details or making careless mistakes at work?

I don't really know if I make careless mistakes, honestly. I mean, maybe? It's hard to say because in advertising sales, a lot of what we do is pretty fluid until the final contract is drawn up. Like, yesterday I was working on this pitch deck for a local car dealership—they want to run a huge campaign for their summer blowout event. They always do these massive inflatable tube men outside the lot, you know the ones that flail around in the wind? I actually think those are kind of terrifying. I drove past one at a different dealership once at night, and the way the streetlights hit it, it looked like a giant flailing monster. I almost swerved into the other lane! But anyway, with the pitch deck, I guess I sometimes miss a typo or two before I send it to my manager to review, but I wouldn't say I have trouble paying attention to details. It's just that there's always so much going on in the office.
Before age 15, did you ever run away from home?

Run away from home? Oh, gosh, no. I mean, my parents were pretty strict, but not in a way that made me want to leave. They were just really focused on academics and extracurriculars. My mom actually made me take piano lessons for six years, which I absolutely hated. I mean, I appreciate it now, I guess, because I can play "Fur Elise" at parties if there's a piano, but back then, it was torture. My teacher, Mr. Henderson, always smelled like peppermint and old coffee, and he had this metronome that just ticked so loudly. Tick, tick, tick... it used to drive me crazy. I actually tried to hide it once in the bench with all the sheet music, but he found it almost immediately. He was so particular about his sheet music, too—everything had to be perfectly organized by composer and era. I'm definitely not that organized, my desk at work is just a pile of sticky notes right now. But yeah, no, I never ran away.
Have you ever gotten in trouble for deliberately hurting, bullying, or intimidating other people?

Me? Bully someone? No, definitely not. I was always the one trying to make sure everyone was included. Like, if someone was sitting alone at lunch, I'd go sit with them. Which actually backfired on me once in middle school because I sat with this girl, Chloe, and she ended up being super clingy. Like, she would follow me to my locker, to the bathroom, everywhere. And she had this weird obsession with horses. Everything she owned had a horse on it—her backpack, her folders, even her socks. I mean, I like animals, but I'm more of a dog person. I actually really want to get a Golden Retriever, but my apartment complex has a strict weight limit for pets, which is so annoying. It's like, 25 pounds. What kind of dog is under 25 pounds? Basically just a glorified cat. And I'm allergic to cats, so that's out. My eyes get all itchy and puffy, it's terrible. So I guess I'm just stuck with plants for now, even though I keep killing my succulents. Everyone says they're impossible to kill, but I somehow manage to overwater them every single time. But yeah, to answer your question, no, I never bullied or hurt anyone on purpose.
As a child, did you often have trouble finishing homework or other tasks because you got distracted?

Oh, definitely. I remember this starting way before high school, actually. Back in elementary school, my teachers were always writing on my report cards that I was a bright kid but I rushed through everything, and that I talked out of turn a lot. I was always forgetting my homework, too. My desk was just a complete disaster zone—it was stuffed to the brim with half-finished papers and worksheets. And those colorful Lisa Frank folders! I don't know if you remember those, but I was completely obsessed with the one that had the neon dolphins on it. I begged my mom to buy me the matching pencil case, but she said it was too expensive, so I had to settle for this plain blue one that I just ended up drawing all over with gel pens anyway. Gel pens were the absolute best back then, especially the sparkly silver ones. They always smeared so badly if you were left-handed, though. I'm right-handed, so it wasn't a huge deal for me, but my best friend Sarah was a lefty and she always had this shiny silver smudge on the side of her hand by the end of the day. It took forever to wash off, too. But yeah, whenever we had to clean out our desks on Friday afternoons, my teachers were always pulling out crumpled, half-done assignments from the very back of mine.
